task: Extended managed MCP handling so a backend entry's `oauth` field can be a structured OAuth client configuration object forwarded verbatim into Claude Desktop's managedMcpServers config, alongside the legacy boolean/enum flag.

component_scope.label: M
component_scope.affected: managed MCP remote fetch/validation (managed-mcp-remote.ts), Claude Desktop config writer with oauth resolution + default/org merge + reconcile (desktop.ts), proxy connect desktop command wiring and logging (index.ts)
component_scope.layers: CLI (command), Service (proxy connectors), External (CodeMie managed-servers API contract + Claude Desktop config surface)

requirements_clarity.label: M
requirements_clarity.gaps: Several policy decisions were resolved in-implementation rather than stated up front: precedence between a structured oauth object, the oauth boolean, and the legacy `auth` enum (resolveDesktopOAuth); whether a malformed oauth object invalidates the whole entry (it does); whether the CLI may correct an auth downgrade (it logs, never rewrites); which bundled defaults may be seeded when the catalog fetch fails. Code also records a known, separately-tracked gap: managed endpoint URL comparison is verbatim, with no trailing-slash or host-case normalization.

technical_risk.label: L
technical_risk.risk_factors: Payload is OAuth client configuration (clientId, authorizationUrl, tokenUrl, scope, callback host/port) that governs how Claude Desktop authenticates to MCP servers; an open index signature deliberately forwards unknown backend keys unvalidated; the writer rewrites a third-party app's config file and can revoke a tenant's org MCP entries if a failed fetch were mistaken for an empty catalog; marker-state (desktop-managed-mcp-state.json) ordering determines whether entries can be orphaned across a crash
technical_risk.mitigation: null-vs-[] contract distinguishes fetch failure from an authoritative empty catalog; a non-empty payload where nothing survives validation returns null; selectDefaultsForFailedFetch seeds nothing that collides with existing config entries; write-ahead union marker plus atomic tmp+rename state write; cloneManagedEntry deep-copies oauth so module-level DEFAULT_MANAGED_MCP_SERVERS cannot be mutated; summarizeManagedOauthShapes surfaces a mass downgrade or validation drop in the daemon log

affected_layers.label: M
layers_changed: External (CodeMie managed-servers API contract + Claude Desktop config file)

key_reasoning.reason: Base M for a new-but-contained validation/forwarding pattern, bumped to L by the authentication/authorization red flag: the forwarded object is OAuth client configuration for Desktop's flow, and the same writer can revoke a tenant's org MCP servers if a failed fetch is misread. The diff shows the risk was answered structurally (null-vs-[] fetch contract, write-ahead marker + atomic rename, deep clone of module-level defaults, downgrade logging without correction) rather than left open.

Three source components in one subsystem: fetch/validation (isValidOAuthConfig, entry-level rejection of malformed oauth, wholesale oauth copy in pickCanonicalFields), the Desktop writer (resolveDesktopOAuth, mergeManagedMcpServers, selectDefaultsForFailedFetch, cloneManagedEntry, summarizeManagedOauthShapes), and the connect-desktop command that wires and logs oauth shape counts. Coordination across CLI and connector layers, but no shared utility or cross-agent impact.

The stated requirement ('forward verbatim') did not settle precedence between oauth object / oauth boolean / legacy auth enum, malformed-object handling, collision precedence between bundled defaults and the org catalog, or failed-fetch seeding — all of which appear as explicitly reasoned decisions in the implementation comments.
6 files (3 source, 3 test) across the proxy command and connectors directories; 1111 insertions against only 22 deletions, i.e. overwhelmingly additive with test coverage carrying most of the volume.

red_flags_applied: Technical Risk bumped from M (3) to L (4): change carries authentication/authorization data — OAuth client configuration (clientId, authorizationUrl, tokenUrl, scope, callback host/port) forwarded into the client that runs the flow.
